dataset.description: Environmental descriptors (water temperature, salinity gradient, pH, turbidity) for all sampling stations will be measured in situ using a range of sensors and probes. Supplementary abiotic and biotic parameters, such as hydrochemical data (DIN, DIP, TN, TP, DOC) and biological analyses (including benthic community structure), are also part of the national monitoring program and can therefore be used as additional indicators of environmental quality and to support further linkage with multi-biomarker approaches. The output of the national monitoring program will be compiled into a database alongside the chemical analysis results for the target pollutants of the Sedi-Q project. Subsequently, a quality-controlled database will be prepared and published in the LATMARE marine monitoring database maintained by LIAE.

distribution.title: The abiotic parameters such as salinity, temperature and dissolved oxygen concentration will be measured in all stations using a CTD probe (SBE 19plus Sea-Cat, Sea-Bird Scientific, USA) at a bottom layer. This data will help identify abiotic parameter linkages with biological and chemical data. All chemical analyses will be analyzed according to the accredited method in local or abroad laboratories.

dataset.title: Field studies and chemical analysis of pollutants in sediments in GoR

dmp.description: Chemical analysis of pollutants in sediments alone does not comprehensively answer whether pollution adversely affects marine organisms. However, it is increasingly important to clarify the relationship between the consequences of potential pollution on organism development and the reduction of biological diversity. Considering the effects of mixtures of substances in general and determining the ecological quality of sediments using an interdisciplinary method solution approach is therefore crucial. This project aims to develop and operationalise interdisciplinary approaches and methods for assessing the ecological risk of sediments in the Gulf of Riga and the ecosystem's environmental quality. Planned results in this project include a) tried and tested interdisciplinary methods in the assessment of sediment quality by combining benthic biodiversity indexes with chemistry, biological effects and experimental studies b) identified negative effects caused by specific chemical compounds on the development of organisms in ecotoxicity tests c) develop sediment quality values to identify polluted and reference areas in the Gulf of Riga. The development and use of such an early warning method will significantly contribute to the assessment of the environmental quality of Latvia's territorial waters, allowing more effective participation in the implementation of the Baltic Sea Action Plan (BSAP) and meeting the requirements of the EU Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD).

project.description: The scientific quality of the project will be based on integrating different disciplines to assess the pollution in aquatic ecosystems in the Gulf of Riga and the linkage of the causes and effects from using different lines of evidence. The proposal combines field- and laboratory-based disciplines covering biology, chemistry, and ecology, these data will be used to assess sediment quality in the Gulf of Riga.
